title: What works at the point of influence—and who the safeguard protects
review_method: Single-pass, purposive, source-linked assessment; not independent double screening or full-text extraction of every study.
mode_note: Evidence modes are not ordered grades, independent experiments, or counts of effective policies.

manuscript.web_update: The v1.3 manuscript integrates this source-linked review. No new fellowship experiments or automatic Atlas empirical-flag upgrades.

source_files.source_name: P4 — Individual dossiers and source ledger — 118 implementations — 20260901.md

sources.title: Nouwens et al. — Dark Patterns after the GDPR
sources.design: Within-person field browsing experiment; 40 US Chrome users; eight consent interfaces
sources.review_depth: Retained prior adjudication; primary abstract rechecked
sources.finding: Removing the first-screen reject option increased cookie acceptance by approximately 22–23 percentage points.
sources.boundary: Interface-induced acceptance is not informed preference alignment or the causal effect of enforcing a statutory ban.

sources.title: Luguri and Strahilevitz — Shining a Light on Dark Patterns
sources.finding: Deceptive interface designs increased acceptance of a questionable service in the tested settings.
sources.boundary: No population electoral outcome or evaluation of an implemented regulatory prohibition; magnitudes not extracted here.

sources.title: Ershov and Morales — Sharing News Left and Right
sources.design: Quasi-experimental analysis of Twitter's October 2020 retweet friction change
sources.finding: The friction reduced news sharing, but did not selectively reduce misleading relative to factual news; responses differed by political orientation.
sources.boundary: Not randomized platform assignment and not WhatsApp forwarding limits. Reduced total circulation is not improved discernment.

sources.title: de Freitas Melo et al. — WhatsApp forwarded-many-times coverage
sources.design: Observational study of 9.8 million messages in 1,101 public Brazilian political groups
sources.review_depth: Retained prior adjudication; primary abstract rechecked
sources.finding: Many duplicate-media appearances lacked the forwarding label even when the item was labelled elsewhere.
sources.boundary: Coverage failure is not an estimate of the limit's effect on delay, authentic exposure, behaviour or harm.

sources.title: de Freitas Melo et al. — Can WhatsApp Counter Misinformation by Limiting Message Forwarding?
sources.design: Diffusion modelling informed by messaging data
sources.finding: Forwarding limits can delay modelled dissemination but need not stop highly viral content.
sources.boundary: Simulation assumptions and selected public-group data; no causal human behavioural estimate.

sources.title: Pennycook et al. — Shifting attention to accuracy can reduce misinformation online
sources.design: Survey experiments and a Twitter field experiment
sources.finding: Accuracy prompts improved sharing discernment in surveys and the average quality of sources subsequently shared in the field.
sources.boundary: Source quality is a proxy; effects on durable agency and adaptive conversation were not measured.

sources.title: Pennycook and Rand — Accuracy prompts are a replicable and generalizable approach
sources.finding: The experimental corpus supports improved sharing discernment on average.
sources.boundary: Studies are not all independent teams; overlap with R008. Do not count pooled datasets twice.

sources.title: Martel et al. — Accuracy-prompt adversarial reanalysis
sources.design: Adversarial collaboration; reanalysis of 21 experiments; approximately 27,000 participants
sources.finding: Estimated sharing-discernment benefits persisted across specifications, including among Republicans, with heterogeneous magnitudes.
sources.boundary: Overlaps R007; mostly stated sharing rather than measured field behaviour. Not a new 27,000-person independent trial.

sources.title: Slaughter et al. — Community Notes and engagement with misleading posts
sources.review_depth: Main-text methods, results, limitations and correction notice checked; supplement/data not reproduced
sources.finding: Estimated repost reduction was larger after a note appeared than over a post's lifetime; lifetime estimates were 11.6% for reposts and 5.5% for views.
sources.boundary: Conditional on observed note/post eligibility, timing and synthetic-control assumptions; not randomized rollout or electoral effects.

sources.title: Chuai et al. — Did the Roll-Out of Community Notes Reduce Engagement?
sources.finding: The rollout analysis did not find an overall reduction in engagement with misinformation.
sources.boundary: Different estimand from post-note attenuation in R009; delays and coverage can reconcile the findings.

sources.title: Roozenbeek et al. — Psychological inoculation improves resilience against misinformation
sources.design: Six online randomized experiments and a YouTube field study
sources.review_depth: Retained prior adjudication; primary abstract rechecked
sources.finding: Brief videos improved immediate recognition of the manipulation techniques taught.
sources.boundary: Recognition within the tested window is not durable resistance, actual sharing, agency or election protection.

sources.title: Biddlestone et al. — Tune in to the prebunking network
sources.finding: Technique detection improved more consistently than discernment; a moving-goalposts treatment also induced generalized distrust.
sources.boundary: Effects vary by technique and outcome; cannot generalize from detection to resistance.

sources.title: Ancina, Zumbrägel and Krämer — Inoculation in a WhatsApp setting
sources.finding: Matched inoculation reduced false-message credibility, without a detected sharing-intention benefit or cross-topic transfer.
sources.boundary: Simulated chats, limited sample and topic scope; not a private-platform field experiment.

sources.title: Pennycook et al. — Inoculation and accuracy prompting in combination
sources.review_depth: Primary abstract and publication metadata checked
sources.finding: Emotional-technique inoculation improved recognition but not truth discernment alone; combining it with accuracy prompting improved discernment through belief in true content.
sources.boundary: Tested combination and stimuli only, not proof that arbitrary policy packages are synergistic; some authors/funding linked to Google.

sources.title: Carey et al. — Prebunking and credible-source corrections increase election credibility
sources.design: Three preregistered online experiments in the US and Brazil
sources.review_depth: Retained prior adjudication; primary abstract rechecked
sources.finding: Factual election-security messages changed confidence, fraud beliefs and accuracy; persistence and context mattered. Forewarning did not supply the presumed extra benefit.
sources.boundary: Messages are not official-source-connected assistants; no voting-access, turnout or agency endpoint.

sources.title: DeVerna et al. — Fact-checking information from LLMs can decrease headline discernment
sources.review_depth: Main text, methods and results checked
sources.finding: The tested LLM fact checks did not improve average discernment; erroneous and uncertain outputs produced harmful item-specific responses.
sources.boundary: One older configuration and 40 headlines. Human comparison was collected a year later; opt-in comparisons are selected, not randomized.

sources.title: Gallegos et al. — AI authorship labels and political persuasion
sources.finding: AI-authorship labels did not significantly change persuasion, perceived accuracy or sharing in the tested policy messages.
sources.boundary: No general zero-effect conclusion, no personalized persistent conversation; label concerns origin rather than veracity.

sources.title: Labeling Synthetic Content — User study
sources.design: Experiment with 911 participants and alternative label designs
sources.finding: Labels improved identification of synthetic origin more readily than engagement-related outcomes.
sources.boundary: Origin recognition is not claim accuracy or resistance to operator steering.

sources.title: Dathathri et al. — Scalable watermarking for identifying LLM outputs
sources.design: Technical watermark evaluation and large-scale product testing
sources.finding: SynthID-Text supports detection of outputs from cooperating generators under tested conditions, with reported utility preservation.
sources.boundary: A watermark does not determine truth, prevent persuasion or cover uncooperative models and all transformations.

sources.title: C2PA Security Considerations, version 2.0
sources.finding: Specifies security assumptions and integrity properties of provenance assertions.
sources.boundary: An authenticated assertion is not truth; no human-effect experiment or democratic-benefit estimate.

sources.title: Chandra et al. — Deepfake-Eval-2024
sources.finding: Detector performance deteriorated on in-the-wild media relative to conventional benchmark settings.
sources.boundary: Out-of-distribution technical detection, not a trial of an election mitigation programme; AUC is not classification accuracy.

sources.title: Prasad, Nahapetyan and Reaves — Characterizing Robocalls through a Five-Year Honeypot
sources.review_depth: Primary author summary and abstract checked
sources.finding: Call patterns and anti-abuse adaptation can be observed over time.
sources.boundary: Changes in call volume do not isolate the effect of STIR/SHAKEN, consent law or one enforcement action.

sources.title: Sherman et al. — User Comprehension of STIR/SHAKEN
sources.finding: Users can misunderstand authentication indicators.
sources.boundary: Authenticating caller identity is not verifying the caller's message or intentions.

sources.title: Edelson, Lauinger and McCoy — A Security Analysis of the Facebook Ad Library
sources.design: Observational adversarial audit of advertising records
sources.finding: The archive exposed substantial gaps in disclosure and coverage.
sources.boundary: Finding missing advertisements demonstrates audit value and incompleteness, not prevention of harm.

sources.title: Dommett and Power — Political advertising transparency
sources.design: Comparative analysis of UK returns and platform ad archives
sources.finding: Different transparency sources provide incomplete and inconsistent views.
sources.boundary: No randomized disclosure treatment or causal reduction in covert influence.

sources.title: Bär et al. — Political advertising delivery on Meta
sources.design: Observational analysis of German political ads and delivery
sources.finding: Actual audience delivery can diverge from targeting inputs, with heterogeneous delivery patterns.
sources.boundary: No causal effect of a targeting restriction or on votes; motivates delivery-level audit, not intent attribution.

sources.title: McCabe et al. — Post-January-6 deplatforming and misinformation
sources.design: Large observational panel around mass account suspension
sources.finding: Misinformation circulation fell among affected networks after the intervention.
sources.boundary: Concurrent January-6 events prevent clean identification of the intervention's causal magnitude; cross-platform displacement unresolved.

sources.title: Gauthier et al. — The political effects of X's feed algorithm
sources.finding: Switching on the algorithm changed selected attitudes; switching it off did not yield a symmetric reversal. Some following choices persisted.
sources.boundary: Pre-existing feed groups differ; asymmetry is not a clean estimate of irreversible agency transfer. No election-result estimate.

sources.title: Guess et al. — How social media feed algorithms affect attitudes and behavior
sources.design: Facebook/Instagram randomized feed intervention during the 2020 US election
sources.finding: Chronological feeds changed use and exposure, without detectable changes in the specified political-attitude measures.
sources.boundary: Null effects are context- and power-bounded; a 2026 erratum was located but its full implications were not adjudicated here.

sources.title: Biega et al. — Operationalizing the Legal Principle of Data Minimization
sources.design: Offline recommender experiments with reduced rating histories
sources.review_depth: Retained prior adjudication; primary abstract rechecked
sources.finding: Recommendation quality depends on the algorithm, user and data budget when histories are reduced.
sources.boundary: No conversation-memory, verified deletion, manipulation, dependency or human autonomy outcome.

sources.title: Aridor, Che and Salz — Privacy regulation and online tracking
sources.design: Quasi-experimental GDPR analysis using an online travel intermediary
sources.finding: Observed data coverage declined, while remaining users could be more trackable, illustrating selection and composition effects.
sources.boundary: One intermediary and legal change; fewer observed cookies is not a universal measure of less concentrated data power.

sources.title: Miller, Lukic and Skiera — GDPR and tracking technologies
sources.finding: Estimated tracker use was lower relative to the counterfactual, with heterogeneous effects; the study did not find the hypothesized concentration increase.
sources.boundary: Relative counterfactual reduction can coexist with absolute growth. Not conversational-memory minimization.

sources.title: Turner et al. — The right to data portability in the IoT
sources.design: 160 privacy policies and four hands-on portability exercises
sources.review_depth: Retained prior adjudication; primary publication summary checked
sources.finding: Receiving a data archive generally did not enable direct transfer or import into a rival service.
sources.boundary: Small, historical IoT exercise; not a current assistant migration trial.

sources.title: Syrmoudis et al. — Data Portability Between Online Services
sources.finding: Implementation barriers limit practical portability despite formal availability.
sources.boundary: No causal restored-agency measure or verified transfer of generative-agent memory and permissions.

sources.title: Allcott et al. — Sources of Market Power in Web Search
sources.design: Field experiments with defaults, active choice and incentivized trial
sources.finding: Defaults, attention and trial experience affect search-engine adoption; a nominal choice screen is not equivalent to a feasible alternative.
sources.boundary: Search is not assistant-state portability; model-based market-share projections are not directly randomized outcomes.

sources.title: CMA — Cloud services market investigation, final report
sources.design: Regulatory market investigation with primary surveys
sources.finding: The investigation identifies concentration and switching/interoperability barriers and proposes further action.
sources.boundary: Diagnosis and recommended remedies are not an estimated causal benefit of implemented remedies.

sources.title: Debenedetti et al. — Defeating Prompt Injections by Design (CaMeL)
sources.design: Technical evaluation of control/data-flow separation and capability policies
sources.review_depth: Main-text threat model, evaluation and limits checked
sources.finding: Hard authorization boundaries constrain external prompt injection under specified assumptions, with a utility trade-off.
sources.boundary: The user/principal and relevant trusted context are assumed trustworthy. This does not protect citizens from an authorized malicious operator.

sources.title: Buçinca, Malaya and Gajos — To Trust or to Think
sources.review_depth: Primary author summary and abstract checked
sources.finding: Cognitive-forcing designs reduced overreliance on erroneous AI advice in bounded decision tasks.
sources.boundary: Benefits and subjective costs were uneven. It does not validate a generic confirmation button or every multi-turn intervention.

sources.title: Poonsiriwong et al. — AI Watchdog
sources.review_depth: Main-text methods, results and limitations checked
sources.finding: A dismissible just-in-time monitor reduced the preregistered secondary rate of AI-steered choices from 71.7% to 53.7%; the primary flagging outcome did not improve.
sources.boundary: Thirty participants per arm; simulated, consequence-free tasks; secondary endpoint; no superiority over forcing established. The monitor was researcher-hosted, not locally deployed.

sources.title: Ibrahim et al. — Warning labels shift perceptions of sycophantic AI, but not its influence
sources.finding: Warnings changed perceptions of the chatbot but did not reliably change self-righteousness or intentions to repair the interpersonal conflict.
sources.boundary: Specified eight-turn dilemmas and self-reports, not observed relationship repair or a proof of zero effect.

sources.title: Salvi, Cuevas and Ribeiro — Commercial Persuasion in AI-Mediated Conversations
sources.review_depth: Main-text methods, outcomes and disclosure comparison checked
sources.finding: Active promotion shifted book selections markedly. Explicit sponsorship disclosure improved detection but did not significantly reduce the selection effect relative to the earlier persuasion condition.
sources.boundary: Disclosure and baseline comparison spans two collection waves; not all five arms were contemporaneously randomized. Simplified purchase stakes; promised books ultimately replaced by monetary bonuses.

sources.title: Fang et al. — Psychosocial Effects of Chatbot Use
sources.finding: The revised analysis reports no significant randomized condition effects; heavier voluntary use and adverse psychosocial measures were associated.
sources.boundary: Voluntary usage is not randomized dosage. Does not show that use caps, memory deletion or labels reduce dependence.

sources.title: Jia et al. — Critical Evaluation of Defenses against Prompt Injection
sources.finding: Defense performance degrades under adaptive attacks and must be compared with utility costs.
sources.boundary: Technical task security, not an estimate of human manipulation or institutional benefit.

sources.title: Hao et al. — AgentDyn
sources.design: Dynamic-environment benchmark; 60 tasks; 560 injections; ten defenses
sources.finding: Dynamic environments reveal limitations missed by static evaluations.
sources.boundary: Benchmark coverage does not set a general release threshold or estimate real-world harm.

sources.title: Ren et al. — MASK
sources.finding: Honesty and factual accuracy can diverge under the benchmark's conditions.
sources.boundary: No validated conversion from benchmark score to human manipulation or a statutory release gate.

sources.title: Duflo et al. — Truth-telling by Third-party Auditors
sources.review_depth: Primary author and NBER summaries checked
sources.finding: An audit-reform package improved reporting truthfulness and reduced pollution in the study.
sources.boundary: Adjacent sector; package changes payment, assignment and cross-checking. Does not isolate AI-audit access or certify DSA audit efficacy.

sources.title: Dyck, Morse and Zingales — Who Blows the Whistle on Corporate Fraud?
sources.design: Observational analysis of reported large-company fraud
sources.finding: Employees, media and other nontraditional actors contribute to detection; information access and incentives matter.
sources.boundary: Selected detected cases, not a randomized whistleblower-protection law or prevention estimate.

sources.title: Longpre et al. — In-House Evaluation Is Not Enough
sources.finding: Proposes standardized flaw reporting, safe harbours and coordination infrastructure.
sources.boundary: A reasoned proposal, not an intervention-effect experiment.

sources.title: Bracamonte et al. — Model-card comprehension
sources.design: Human study of alternative model-card presentation
sources.finding: Documentation design affects users' understanding and confidence.
sources.boundary: Comprehension is not oversight that changes deployer behaviour or prevents harm.

sources.title: NIST — Generative AI Profile 600-1
sources.finding: Organizes proposed risk-management actions across the AI lifecycle.
sources.boundary: No measured effect of adopting the profile; not proof of the whole policy package.

sources.title: NIST — AI Agent Standards Initiative
sources.finding: Identity, authorization, interoperability and security evaluation are explicit workstreams.
sources.boundary: An initiative and research agenda, not evidence that a particular authorization design preserves human agency.

sources.title: ISO — ISO/IEC 42001:2023
sources.review_depth: Official overview checked; paid standard not reviewed
sources.finding: Defines an organizational management-system standard.
sources.boundary: A certificate is not an independently estimated reduction in manipulation or proof of model safety.

sources.title: Validation of challenges in ISO/IEC 42001 adoption in logistics
sources.finding: Identifies perceived adoption barriers including training and integration.
sources.boundary: Validating adoption challenges does not estimate certification's safety effects.

sources.title: European Commission — GPAI Code of Practice
sources.finding: Provides a voluntary route for demonstrating compliance with relevant GPAI obligations.
sources.boundary: Legal/compliance architecture, not causal efficacy evidence. Stronger governance language does not repair an unvalidated metric.

sources.title: European Commission — AI Act implementation and amended timetable
sources.finding: Reports the AI Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026 and changed high-risk application dates.
sources.boundary: The old assumption that Annex III duties generally apply from August 2026 requires correction. Primary consolidated provisions still need clause-level legal review.

sources.title: TSE — Resolution 23.755/2026
sources.finding: Regulates synthetic electoral content, specified blackout periods and AI-mediated recommendations.
sources.boundary: A rule's adoption does not establish compliance, reach prevented, or effects; many relevant 2026 outcomes remain prospective.

sources.title: TSE — Portaria 463/2026
sources.finding: Requires specified services to document electoral-risk mitigations and compliance plans.
sources.boundary: Submitted plans and indicators are administrative outputs, not independently established mitigation effects.

sources.title: European Commission — DSA election-risk guidelines
sources.finding: Recommends measures for designated large services before, during and after elections.
sources.boundary: Not an outcome evaluation; each removal, disclosure or escalation measure has its own estimand.

sources.title: ECAT — DSA researcher-access FAQs
sources.finding: Provides routes and safeguards for independent systemic-risk research access.
sources.boundary: Access rights alone do not establish usable access, valid findings, regulator action or harm reduction.

sources.title: European Commission — EU model AI procurement clauses
sources.finding: Provides contractual tools for specifying provider obligations and public-buyer oversight.
sources.boundary: No causal estimate that inserting clauses creates retained institutional capability or enforceable exit.

sources.title: CAC — Interim Measures for Generative AI Services
sources.finding: Specifies provider, content, data and security-assessment duties for covered services.
sources.boundary: State control or compliance cannot be treated as democratic agency protection. Not a causal efficacy study or a complete review of subsequent amendments.

sources.title: Perset and Fialho Esposito — How are AI developers managing risks?
sources.review_depth: Official abstract and framework pages checked
sources.finding: Documents reported risk-management practices across participating organizations.
sources.boundary: Self-selection and self-report; no untreated comparison or independent safety effect. Report and organization counts differ.

sources.title: OECD — Hiroshima AI reporting framework version 2.0
sources.finding: Expands and streamlines participation and reporting.
sources.boundary: More reports or pledges are not more effective mitigations.

sources.title: Government of Canada — Algorithmic Impact Assessment
sources.finding: Documents an administrative risk-assessment and mitigation process.
sources.boundary: Tool completion is not an estimate of appeal effectiveness or agency preservation.

sources.title: Green and Chen — Algorithmic risk assessments and human government decisions
sources.finding: Risk-assessment information can alter the weights people place on decision factors.
sources.boundary: Lay experimental tasks, not actual bureaucratic outcomes; supports a risk mechanism rather than a tested governance remedy.

sources.title: Liu, Zhang and Liang — Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search
sources.design: Audit of citation support in generative search
sources.finding: Citation presence and actual evidentiary support diverged in evaluated systems.
sources.boundary: Measurement of citation failure, not a test that retrieval automatically improves human decisions.

sources.title: Spatharioti et al. — AI-assisted search and decision accuracy
sources.finding: Users could overrely on erroneous LLM answers; confidence-oriented interface cues improved specified error-detection/decision outcomes.
sources.boundary: Bounded product decisions and interface design; not general agent authorization or durable agency.

sources.title: Nestaas, Debenedetti and Tramèr — Adversarial Search Engine Optimization
sources.design: Technical adversarial evaluation of AI-mediated recommendations
sources.finding: Retrieved content can steer model recommendations under tested conditions.
sources.boundary: Risk evidence, not proof that disclosure, a loyalty audit or a market remedy is effective; offensive payloads excluded.

sources.title: Katsaros et al. — Reconsideration prompts for offensive tweets
sources.finding: Context-specific prompts reduced offensive posting in the tested setting.
sources.boundary: Not generic friction, factual discernment or manipulation; supports testing targeted rather than blanket interruptions.
